import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sato–Tate conjecture

The Sato–Tate conjecture describes the distribution of Frobenius traces of a non-CM elliptic
curve. The original conjecture over `ℚ` is stated below. The broader number-field, modular-form,
and higher-genus variants require arithmetic-geometric notions not yet available in Mathlib.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Sato–Tate conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sato%E2%80%93Tate_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace SatoTateConjecture

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped Real Topology

/-- Reduction of a rational number modulo `p`. At the finitely many primes dividing the
 denominator this takes Mathlib's totalized inverse; those primes do not affect the limit. -/
def rationalReduction (x : ℚ) (p : ℕ) : ZMod p :=
  (x.num : ZMod p) * (x.den : ZMod p)⁻¹

/-- The affine points of the coefficientwise reduction modulo `p` of a rational Weierstrass
model. -/
def affinePoints (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) (p : ℕ) :=
  {P : ZMod p × ZMod p |
    P.2 ^ 2 + rationalReduction E.a₁ p * P.1 * P.2 + rationalReduction E.a₃ p * P.2 =
      P.1 ^ 3 + rationalReduction E.a₂ p * P.1 ^ 2 +
        rationalReduction E.a₄ p * P.1 + rationalReduction E.a₆ p}

/-- The number of points on the reduction of `E` modulo `p`, including the point at infinity. -/
noncomputable def numberOfPoints (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) (p : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card (affinePoints E p) + 1

/-- A rational elliptic curve has complex multiplication exactly when its `j`-invariant is one
of the thirteen rational CM `j`-invariants. -/
def HasComplexMultiplication (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic] : Prop :=
  E.j ∈ ({0, 1728, -3375, 8000, -32768, 54000, 287496, -884736,
    -12288000, 16581375, -884736000, -147197952000,
    -262537412640768000} : Finset ℚ)

/-- The Frobenius angle `θ_p ∈ [0, π]`, obtained from
`p + 1 - #E(𝔽_p) = 2 √p cos θ_p`. The totalized `arccos` gives harmless arbitrary values at
finitely many primes where the chosen rational model does not reduce coefficientwise. -/
noncomputable def frobeniusAngle (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.arccos (((p : ℝ) + 1 - numberOfPoints E p) / (2 * Real.sqrt p))

/--
The Sato–Tate conjecture for a non-CM elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$. If $N_p$ counts the points
of the reduction of $E$ modulo $p$, including infinity, and
$p+1-N_p=2\sqrt p\cos(\theta_p)$ with $0\leq\theta_p\leq\pi$, then for every
$0\leq\alpha<\beta\leq\pi$,
$$
 \lim_{N\to\infty}
 \frac{\#\{p\leq N:p\text{ prime},\ \alpha\leq\theta_p\leq\beta\}}
      {\#\{p\leq N:p\text{ prime}\}}
 =\frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta\sin^2\theta\,d\theta.
$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 14]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic]
    (hE : ¬ HasComplexMultiplication E) (α β : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β)
    (hβ : β ≤ Real.pi) :
    Tendsto
      (fun N : ℕ =>
        (((Finset.range (N + 1)).filter fun p =>
          p.Prime ∧ α ≤ frobeniusAngle E p ∧ frobeniusAngle E p ≤ β).card : ℝ) /
          (N.primeCounting : ℝ))
      atTop
      (𝓝 ((2 / Real.pi) * ∫ θ in α..β, Real.sin θ ^ 2)) := by
  sorry

end SatoTateConjecture

/-!
# Sato–Tate conjecture

The Sato–Tate conjecture describes the distribution of Frobenius traces of a non-CM elliptic
curve over the rational numbers. The original conjecture is now a theorem. There are related
versions for elliptic curves over other number fields, modular forms, and higher-genus curves.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sato–Tate conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sato%E2%80%93Tate_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

namespace SatoTateConjecture

open Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- An integral short Weierstrass model $y^2=x^3+Ax+B$ of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$.
Every elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ has such a model. -/
structure IntegralModel where
  A : ℤ
  B : ℤ
  discriminant_ne_zero : 4 * A ^ 3 + 27 * B ^ 2 ≠ 0

namespace IntegralModel

/-- The $j$-invariant of an integral short Weierstrass model. -/
noncomputable def j (E : IntegralModel) : ℚ :=
  6912 * E.A ^ 3 / (4 * E.A ^ 3 + 27 * E.B ^ 2)

/-- A rational elliptic curve is non-CM exactly when its rational $j$-invariant is not one of the
thirteen rational singular moduli. -/
def IsNonCM (E : IntegralModel) : Prop :=
  E.j ∉ ({0, 1728, -3375, 8000, -32768, 54000, 287496, -884736, -12288000,
    16581375, -884736000, -147197952000, -262537412640768000} : Set ℚ)

/-- The number of points, including the point at infinity, on the reduction modulo `p` of an
integral short Weierstrass model. -/
noncomputable def pointCount (E : IntegralModel) (p : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ({P : ZMod p × ZMod p | P.2 ^ 2 = P.1 ^ 3 + E.A * P.1 + E.B} : Set _).ncard + 1

/-- The angle $\theta_p\in[0,\pi]$ determined by
$p+1-\#E(\mathbb F_p)=2\sqrt p\cos(\theta_p)$. -/
noncomputable def frobeniusAngle (E : IntegralModel) (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.arccos (((p : ℤ) + 1 - E.pointCount p : ℤ) / (2 * Real.sqrt p))

end IntegralModel

/--
The Sato–Tate conjecture for a non-CM elliptic curve $E/\mathbb Q$. If $\theta_p\in[0,\pi]$
is defined by
$$p+1-\#E(\mathbb F_p)=2\sqrt p\cos(\theta_p),$$
then for every $0\leq\alpha<\beta\leq\pi$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}
  \frac{\#\{p\leq N:\ p\text{ prime},\ \alpha\leq\theta_p\leq\beta\}}
       {\#\{p\leq N:\ p\text{ prime}\}}
 =\frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta\sin^2\theta\,d\theta.$$
The model's point count includes the point at infinity. Bad primes are included; their finite
number does not affect the limit. This conjecture is now a theorem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 14]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture (E : IntegralModel) (hE : E.IsNonCM)
    (α β : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β) (hβ : β ≤ Real.pi) :
    Tendsto
      (fun N : ℕ ↦
        ((((Finset.range (N + 1)).filter fun p ↦
            p.Prime ∧ α ≤ E.frobeniusAngle p ∧ E.frobeniusAngle p ≤ β).card : ℝ) /
          (((Finset.range (N + 1)).filter Nat.Prime).card : ℝ)))
      atTop
      (𝓝 ((2 / Real.pi) * ∫ θ in α..β, Real.sin θ ^ 2)) := by
  sorry

end SatoTateConjecture

Elliptic curves over Q are represented by integral short Weierstrass models y^2 = x^3 + Ax + B with nonzero discriminant. Every elliptic curve over Q admits such a model, and changing the integral model affects only finitely many bad-prime reductions.
Because no elliptic-curve CM predicate exists, non-CM over Q is expressed exactly by excluding the thirteen rational singular moduli from the model's rational j-invariant.

Prime counts use Finset.range (N+1), hence include exactly primes p <= N. Bad primes are retained, as in the decomposition notes; they are finite and do not alter the limit.
The interval is closed at both endpoints, exactly as the source states, while the hypotheses retain 0 <= alpha < beta <= pi.
Solved variants were assigned research-solved status where stated; only the original rational variant could be formalized faithfully with available primitives.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sato–Tate conjecture

Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication. For a prime $p$
let $N_p$ be the number of points of the reduction of $E$ modulo $p$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ (including
the point at infinity), and define $\theta_p \in [0, \pi]$ by
$p + 1 - N_p = 2\sqrt{p}\cos\theta_p$. The **Sato–Tate conjecture** states that the angles
$\theta_p$ are equidistributed with respect to the measure $\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$:
for all $0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\#\{p \le N : \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta\,d\theta.$$

This file also states the generalisations to elliptic curves over totally real fields (proved by
Clozel, Harris, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor, and Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor), to
elliptic curves over arbitrary number fields (open), and to non-CM holomorphic newforms of weight
at least two (proved by Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor).

## Implementation notes

* Elliptic curves are given by a Weierstrass equation with integral coefficients (a hypothesis
  `E.IsIntegral ℤ`, resp. `E.IsIntegral (𝓞 K)`). Every elliptic curve is isomorphic to one given by
  an integral Weierstrass equation, and the reduction of such an equation modulo a prime of good
  reduction of the equation is the reduction of the curve. The equation is bad at only finitely many
  primes, and finitely many primes do not affect the limits below.
* Complex multiplication is not in Mathlib. We say that an elliptic curve over a field `K` has
  complex multiplication if, for some embedding `K →+* ℂ`, its `j`-invariant is a singular modulus,
  that is a value `j(τ)` of the modular `j`-function at an imaginary quadratic point `τ`. For a
  number field `K` this is equivalent to the endomorphism ring of `E` over an algebraic closure of
  `K` being larger than `ℤ`.
* Mathlib has neither Hecke operators nor newforms. As in `ModularityConjecture.lean`, a normalised
  eigenform is a cusp form for `Γ₀(N)` whose `q`-expansion coefficients satisfy the Hecke relations.
  Such a form has the same Hecke eigenvalues at all primes `p ∤ N` as a unique newform, so the
  statement is equivalent to the one for newforms.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sato–Tate conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sato%E2%80%93Tate_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- L. Clozel, M. Harris, R. Taylor, *Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois
  representations*, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008).
- M. Harris, N. Shepherd-Barron, R. Taylor, *A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and potential
  automorphy*, Ann. of Math. 171 (2010).
- T. Barnet-Lamb, D. Geraghty, M. Harris, R. Taylor, *A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and
  potential automorphy II*, Publ. RIMS 47 (2011).
- K. Ribet, *Galois representations attached to eigenforms with Nebentypus*, LNM 601 (1977).
-/

namespace SatoTateConjecture

open Filter Real Topology WeierstrassCurve
open scoped UpperHalfPlane

/- ### The Sato–Tate measure -/

/-- The mass $\frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta\,d\theta$ that the Sato–Tate measure
gives to the interval $[\alpha, \beta]$. -/
noncomputable def satoTateMeasure (α β : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (2 / π) * ∫ θ in α..β, sin θ ^ 2

/- ### Complex multiplication -/

/-- The modular `j`-function $j = 1728 E_4^3 / (E_4^3 - E_6^2)$ on the upper half-plane, where
`E_4` and `E_6` are the Eisenstein series of level one normalised to have constant term `1`. -/
noncomputable def jFunction (τ : ℍ) : ℂ :=
  1728 * ModularForm.E (k := 4) (by norm_num) τ ^ 3 /
    (ModularForm.E (k := 4) (by norm_num) τ ^ 3 - ModularForm.E (k := 6) (by norm_num) τ ^ 2)

/-- A complex number is a *singular modulus* if it is the value of the modular `j`-function at a
point `τ` of the upper half-plane that is imaginary quadratic, i.e. that satisfies a quadratic
equation with integer coefficients. -/
def IsSingularModulus (z : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ τ : ℍ, (∃ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 ∧ a * (τ : ℂ) ^ 2 + b * τ + c = 0) ∧ jFunction τ = z

/-- An elliptic curve `E` over a field `K` embedding into `ℂ` (for instance a number field) has
*complex multiplication* if its `j`-invariant is a singular modulus, that is, if it is the
`j`-invariant of a complex elliptic curve `ℂ / Λ` whose lattice `Λ` has complex multiplication.

closure of `K` is strictly larger than `ℤ`. -/

  ∃ σ : K →+* ℂ, IsSingularModulus (σ E.j)

/- ### Elliptic curves over `ℚ` -/

section Rat

variable (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsIntegral ℤ]

/-- The number of points, including the point at infinity, of the reduction modulo `p` of an
elliptic curve `E` over `ℚ` given by an integral Weierstrass equation. At primes of good reduction
of the equation this is `N_p = #E(𝔽_p)`. -/
noncomputable def numPoints (p : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card ((E.integralModel ℤ).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p))).toAffine.Point

/-- The Sato–Tate angle `θ_p ∈ [0, π]` of `E` at a prime `p`, defined by
$p + 1 - N_p = 2\sqrt{p}\cos\theta_p$. -/
noncomputable def theta (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  arccos ((p + 1 - numPoints E p) / (2 * √p))

@[category API, AMS 11 14]
theorem theta_mem_Icc (p : ℕ) : theta E p ∈ Set.Icc 0 π :=
  ⟨arccos_nonneg _, arccos_le_pi _⟩

@[category API, AMS 11 14]
theorem cos_theta (p : ℕ) (h : |(p + 1 - numPoints E p : ℝ) / (2 * √p)| ≤ 1) :
    cos (theta E p) = (p + 1 - numPoints E p) / (2 * √p) :=
  cos_arccos (abs_le.1 h).1 (abs_le.1 h).2

/-- **Sato–Tate conjecture.** Let `E` be an elliptic curve over `ℚ` without complex
multiplication. For a prime `p`, let `N_p` be the number of points of the reduction of `E` modulo

`0 ≤ α < β ≤ π`,

  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta\,d\theta.$$

and Taylor (2011). -/

    {α β : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β) (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
      ({p | p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N ∧ theta E p ∈ Set.Icc α β}.ncard : ℝ) /
        {p | p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N}.ncard)
      atTop (𝓝 (satoTateMeasure α β)) := by
  sorry

discriminant is a unit at `v`. -/

of the integral Weierstrass equation of `E`. At places of good reduction of the equation this is

/- ### Modular forms -/

section ModularForms

open CongruenceSubgroup ModularFormClass

variable {N : ℕ} {k : ℤ} (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k)

/-- The `n`-th Fourier coefficient `a_n(f)` of a cusp form `f` for `Γ₀(N)`, i.e. the coefficient
of `q ^ n` in its `q`-expansion, where `q = exp (2 π i τ)`. -/
noncomputable def modularFormAn (n : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  (qExpansion 1 f).coeff n

/-- A cusp form `f = ∑ a_n q ^ n` of weight `k` for `Γ₀(N)` (with trivial character) is a
*normalised eigenform* if `a_1 = 1` and its coefficients satisfy the Hecke relations
`a_{mn} = a_m a_n` for coprime `m, n`, `a_{p^r} = a_p a_{p^{r-1}} - p^{k-1} a_{p^{r-2}}` for primes
`p ∤ N`, and `a_{p^r} = a_p^r` for primes `p ∣ N`. Equivalently, `f` is an eigenvector of all Hecke
operators with `a_1 = 1`; see Proposition 5.8.5 of Diamond and Shurman, *A First Course in Modular
Forms*. Such a form has the same coefficients `a_p`, `p ∤ N`, as a unique newform. -/
def IsNormalisedEigenform : Prop :=
  modularFormAn f 1 = 1 ∧
  (∀ m n : ℕ, m.Coprime n → modularFormAn f (m * n) = modularFormAn f m * modularFormAn f n) ∧
  (∀ p r : ℕ, p.Prime → 2 ≤ r → ¬ p ∣ N →
    modularFormAn f (p ^ r) =
      modularFormAn f p * modularFormAn f (p ^ (r - 1)) -
        (p : ℂ) ^ (k - 1) * modularFormAn f (p ^ (r - 2))) ∧
  (∀ p r : ℕ, p.Prime → 2 ≤ r → p ∣ N → modularFormAn f (p ^ r) = modularFormAn f p ^ r)

/-- A cusp form `f = ∑ a_n q ^ n` has *complex multiplication* (is a *CM form*) if there is an
imaginary quadratic field `ℚ(√d)`, `d < 0`, such that `a_p = 0` for all but finitely many primes
`p` that are inert in `ℚ(√d)`; for odd primes `p ∤ d`, `p` is inert if and only if `d` is not a
square modulo `p`. By a theorem of Ribet, a newform has this property if and only if it is the
theta series attached to a Hecke character of an imaginary quadratic field. -/
def IsCMForm : Prop :=
  ∃ d : ℤ, d < 0 ∧ {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ¬ IsSquare (d : ZMod p) ∧ modularFormAn f p ≠ 0}.Finite

/-- The Sato–Tate angle `θ_p ∈ [0, π]` of a normalised eigenform `f = ∑ a_n q ^ n` of weight `k`
at a prime `p`, defined by `a_p = 2 p ^ ((k - 1) / 2) cos θ_p`. For `p ∤ N` the coefficient `a_p`
is real and satisfies `|a_p| ≤ 2 p ^ ((k - 1) / 2)` (Deligne), so `θ_p` is well defined. -/
noncomputable def thetaForm (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  arccos ((modularFormAn f p).re / (2 * (p : ℝ) ^ (((k : ℝ) - 1) / 2)))

/-- **Sato–Tate conjecture for modular forms.** Let `f = ∑ a_n q ^ n` be a normalised eigenform
(newform) of weight `k ≥ 2` and level `N ≥ 1` with trivial character and without complex
multiplication. For a prime `p ∤ N` define `θ_p ∈ [0, π]` by `a_p = 2 p ^ ((k - 1) / 2) cos θ_p`.
Then for all real numbers `0 ≤ α < β ≤ π`,
$$\lim_{X\to\infty}
  \frac{\#\{p \le X : p \nmid N,\ \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le X : p \nmid N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta\,d\theta.$$
Proved by Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor (2011). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture.variants.modular_forms (hN : N ≠ 0) (hk : 2 ≤ k)
    (hf : IsNormalisedEigenform f) (hCM : ¬ IsCMForm f)
    {α β : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β) (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun X : ℕ ↦
      ({p | p.Prime ∧ ¬ p ∣ N ∧ p ≤ X ∧ thetaForm f p ∈ Set.Icc α β}.ncard : ℝ) /
        {p | p.Prime ∧ ¬ p ∣ N ∧ p ≤ X}.ncard)
      atTop (𝓝 (satoTateMeasure α β)) := by
  sorry

end ModularForms

end SatoTateConjecture

# Sato–Tate conjecture

Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication. For a prime $p$
let $N_p$ be the number of points of $E$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ (including the point at infinity)

Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (2008) under a mild hypothesis, and in general by Barnet-Lamb,
Geraghty, Harris and Taylor (2011), who also proved the analogue for non-CM holomorphic newforms of
weight at least two. The analogue over an arbitrary number field is open in general.

* Mathlib has no notion of complex multiplication. We say that a Weierstrass curve `E` over a

  good reduction of the chosen model; there are only finitely many other primes, so this does not
  change the limits.

-/

open SatoTateConjecture

/- ### Complex multiplication -/

section ComplexMultiplication

variable {L : Type*} [Field L] [DecidableEq L]

/-- A group endomorphism `φ` of the points of a Weierstrass curve `W` over a field `L` is an
*isogeny* (a non-zero endomorphism of `W` as an algebraic group defined over `L`) if it is given
by rational functions of the affine coordinates: there are polynomials
`f₁, g₁, f₂, g₂ ∈ L[X][Y]` such that for all but finitely many affine points `(x, y)` of `W`, the

is a group homomorphism because it agrees with `φ` on a dense open set. Conversely, every non-zero
isogeny `W → W` has this form. -/
def IsIsogeny (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine L) (φ : W.Point →+ W.Point) : Prop :=
  ∃ f₁ g₁ f₂ g₂ : L[X][Y], ∀ᶠ P in cofinite, ∀ {x y : L} (h : W.Nonsingular x y),

      ∃ h' : W.Nonsingular (f₁.evalEval x y / g₁.evalEval x y) (f₂.evalEval x y / g₂.evalEval x y),

/-- The identity is an isogeny. -/

theorem isIsogeny_id (W : WeierstrassCurve.Affine L) : IsIsogeny W (AddMonoidHom.id W.Point) := by
  refine ⟨C X, 1, X, 1, Eventually.of_forall fun P x y h hP ↦ ?_⟩
  simp only [evalEval, eval_one, ne_eq, one_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true, eval_C, eval_X, div_one,
    true_and]
  exact ⟨h, hP⟩

open scoped WeierstrassCurve.Affine Classical in
/-- An elliptic curve `E` over a field `K` *has complex multiplication* if its endomorphism ring

end ComplexMultiplication

noncomputable def satoTateIntegral (α β : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 / π * ∫ θ in α..β, sin θ ^ 2

theorem satoTateIntegral_zero_pi : satoTateIntegral 0 π = 1 := by
  rw [satoTateIntegral, integral_sin_sq]
  simp only [sin_zero, cos_zero, mul_one, sin_pi, cos_pi, mul_neg, neg_zero, sub_self,

  field_simp

open ModularFormClass CongruenceSubgroup

variable {N : ℕ} {k : ℤ}

noncomputable def CuspForm.coeff (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) (n : ℕ) : ℂ :=

def CuspForm.IsNormalisedEigenform (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) : Prop :=

    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ¬ p ∣ N → ¬ p ∣ M → ψ p * f.coeff p = f.coeff p

end ModularForms

end SatoTateConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sato–Tate conjecture

Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication. For a prime $p$
let $N_p$ be the number of points of the reduction of $E$ modulo $p$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$, and
define $\theta_p \in [0, \pi]$ by $p + 1 - N_p = 2\sqrt{p}\cos\theta_p$. The **Sato–Tate
conjecture** states that the angles $\theta_p$ are equidistributed with respect to the measure
$\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$ on $[0, \pi]$: for all $0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\#\{p \le N : \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta\,d\theta.$$

The conjecture and its generalisation to totally real fields were proved by Clozel, Harris,
Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (2008, under a mild hypothesis) and by Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris
and Taylor (2011). The latter also proved the analogue for non-CM holomorphic cuspidal newforms of
weight at least two. The analogue for elliptic curves over an arbitrary number field is open.

## Formalisation notes

* Mathlib has no notion of the endomorphism ring of an elliptic curve. Complex multiplication is
  therefore defined analytically: an elliptic curve `E` over a field `K` has complex
  multiplication if, for some (equivalently, every) embedding `σ : K → ℂ`, `σ(j(E))` is a
  *singular modulus*, i.e. `σ(j(E)) = j(τ)` for an imaginary quadratic point `τ` of the upper
  half-plane, where `j = 1728 E₄³ / (E₄³ - E₆²)` is the modular `j`-function.
* The reduction of `E` at a finite place `v` is the reduction of a `v`-minimal model of `E`
  (`WeierstrassCurve.minimal` and `WeierstrassCurve.reduction` from Mathlib). Its number of
  points is the number of solutions of the Weierstrass equation over the residue field plus one
  (the point at infinity).
* Over `ℚ` the statement counts all primes, as in the source. At the finitely many primes of
  bad reduction the angle `θ_p` is still defined (there `a_p ∈ {0, ±1}`) and these primes do
  not affect the limit. Over a number field the statement counts places of good reduction, ordered
  by norm.
* A normalised Hecke eigenform is defined through the multiplicative relations satisfied by its
  Fourier coefficients (Diamond–Shurman, Proposition 5.8.5), since Mathlib has no Hecke
  operators. A cusp form has complex multiplication if it is fixed by a twist by a non-trivial
  Dirichlet character (Ribet).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Sato–Tate conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sato%E2%80%93Tate_conjecture)
- Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*,
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics
- L. Clozel, M. Harris, R. Taylor, *Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l
  Galois representations*, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008), https://doi.org/10.1007/s10240-008-0016-1
- M. Harris, N. Shepherd-Barron, R. Taylor, *A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and potential
  automorphy*, Ann. of Math. 171 (2010), https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2010.171.779
- T. Barnet-Lamb, D. Geraghty, M. Harris, R. Taylor, *A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and
  potential automorphy II*, Publ. RIMS 47 (2011), https://doi.org/10.2977/PRIMS/31
- K. Ribet, *Galois representations attached to eigenforms with Nebentypus*, LNM 601 (1977)
- [F. Diamond and J. Shurman, *A First Course in Modular Forms*][diamondshurman2005]
- [J. Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*][silverman2009]
-/

namespace SatoTateConjecture

open Filter IsDedekindDomain NumberField Real SatoTateConjecture
open scoped Topology UpperHalfPlane

/- ### Complex multiplication -/

open ModularForm in
/-- The modular `j`-function `j(τ) = 1728 E₄(τ)³ / (E₄(τ)³ - E₆(τ)²)` on the upper half-plane,
where `E₄` and `E₆` are the normalised Eisenstein series of level one (constant term `1`). -/
noncomputable def jFunction (τ : ℍ) : ℂ :=
  1728 * E (k := 4) (by norm_num) τ ^ 3 /
    (E (k := 4) (by norm_num) τ ^ 3 - E (k := 6) (by norm_num) τ ^ 2)

/-- A point `τ` of the upper half-plane is a *CM point* if it is imaginary quadratic, i.e. a root
of a quadratic polynomial with integer coefficients. -/
def IsCMPoint (τ : ℍ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 ∧ a * (τ : ℂ) ^ 2 + b * (τ : ℂ) + c = 0

/-- The point `i` is a CM point. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem isCMPoint_I : IsCMPoint UpperHalfPlane.I :=
  ⟨1, 0, 1, one_ne_zero, by simp⟩

/-- An elliptic curve `E` over a field `K` has *complex multiplication* if its `j`-invariant is a
singular modulus: for some embedding `σ : K → ℂ` there is a CM point `τ` with
`σ(j(E)) = j(τ)`. Equivalently, `E` is isomorphic over `ℂ` to `ℂ / (ℤ + τℤ)` with `τ` imaginary
quadratic, i.e. the endomorphism ring of `E` over an algebraic closure of `K` is larger than
`ℤ`. Since the singular moduli are permuted by `Gal(ℚ̄ / ℚ)`, the choice of `σ` is irrelevant. -/
def WeierstrassCurve.HasComplexMultiplication {K : Type*} [Field K] (E : WeierstrassCurve K)
    [E.IsElliptic] : Prop :=
  ∃ (σ : K →+* ℂ) (τ : ℍ), IsCMPoint τ ∧ σ E.j = jFunction τ

/- ### Point counts, Frobenius angles and the Sato–Tate measure -/

/-- The number of points of a Weierstrass curve `W` over a field `F`: the number of solutions of
the (affine) Weierstrass equation plus one for the point at infinity. -/
noncomputable def numPoints {F : Type*} [Field F] (W : WeierstrassCurve F) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {P : F × F // W.toAffine.Equation P.1 P.2} + 1

/-- The number of points of the reduction of a Weierstrass curve `E` over the fraction field `K`
of a discrete valuation ring `R`: a minimal model of `E` over `R` is reduced modulo the maximal
ideal of `R`, and its points over the residue field are counted. -/
noncomputable def numPointsReduction (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] {K : Type*} [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (E : WeierstrassCurve K) : ℕ :=
  numPoints ((E.minimal R).reduction R)

/-- The angle `θ ∈ [0, π]` attached to an integer `a` and a natural number `q` by
`a = 2 √q cos θ`. For `a` a trace of Frobenius over `𝔽_q` the Hasse bound gives `|a| ≤ 2 √q`,
so `θ` is well defined. -/
noncomputable def frobeniusAngle (a : ℤ) (q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  arccos (a / (2 * √(q : ℝ)))

@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem frobeniusAngle_mem_Icc (a : ℤ) (q : ℕ) : frobeniusAngle a q ∈ Set.Icc 0 π :=
  ⟨arccos_nonneg _, arccos_le_pi _⟩

/-- The Sato–Tate measure `(2 / π) sin² θ dθ` of the interval `[α, β]`. -/
noncomputable def satoTateMeasure (α β : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2 / π * ∫ θ in α..β, sin θ ^ 2

/-- The closed form of the Sato–Tate measure of `[α, β]` given in the source. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem satoTateMeasure_eq (α β : ℝ) :
    satoTateMeasure α β = (β - α + sin α * cos α - sin β * cos β) / π := by
  rw [satoTateMeasure, integral_sin_sq]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- The Sato–Tate measure is a probability measure on `[0, π]`. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem satoTateMeasure_zero_pi : satoTateMeasure 0 π = 1 := by
  rw [satoTateMeasure_eq]
  simp [pi_ne_zero]

/- ### Elliptic curves over `ℚ` -/

/-- The trace of Frobenius `a_p(E) = p + 1 - N_p` of a Weierstrass curve `E` over `ℚ` at a prime
`p`, where `N_p` is the number of points over `𝔽_p` of the reduction modulo `p` of a minimal model
of `E` at `p`. -/
noncomputable def WeierstrassCurve.apRat (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ℤ :=
  p + 1 - numPointsReduction ℤ_[p] (E.baseChange ℚ_[p])

/-- The Frobenius angle `θ_p ∈ [0, π]` of a Weierstrass curve `E` over `ℚ` at a prime `p`,
defined by `p + 1 - N_p = 2 √p cos θ_p`. -/
noncomputable def WeierstrassCurve.thetaRat (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) (p : Nat.Primes) : ℝ :=
  haveI : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime := ⟨p.2⟩
  frobeniusAngle (E.apRat p) p

/--
**Sato–Tate conjecture.** Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex
multiplication. For a prime $p$ let $N_p$ be the number of points of $E$ modulo $p$ over
$\mathbb{F}_p$ and define $\theta_p \in [0, \pi]$ by $p + 1 - N_p = 2\sqrt{p}\cos\theta_p$.
Then for all real numbers $0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\#\{p \le N : \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta\,d\theta.$$

This is a theorem of Clozel, Harris, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (2008), completed by
Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor (2011).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 14]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic]
    (hE : ¬ E.HasComplexMultiplication) {α β : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β) (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
        ({p : Nat.Primes | (p : ℕ) ≤ N ∧ E.thetaRat p ∈ Set.Icc α β}.ncard : ℝ) /
          Nat.primeCounting N)
      atTop (𝓝 (satoTateMeasure α β)) := by
  sorry

/- ### Elliptic curves over number fields -/

section NumberFields

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]

/-- A Weierstrass curve `E` over a number field `K` has good reduction at a finite place `v` if
a `v`-minimal model of `E` has discriminant of valuation zero at `v`. -/
def WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction (E : WeierstrassCurve K) (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :
    Prop :=
  WeierstrassCurve.IsGoodReduction (v.valuation K).integer (E.minimal (v.valuation K).integer)

/-- The trace of Frobenius `a_v(E) = q_v + 1 - N_v` of a Weierstrass curve `E` over a number field
`K` at a finite place `v`, where `q_v` is the norm of `v` and `N_v` is the number of points over
the residue field of the reduction at `v` of a `v`-minimal model of `E`. -/
noncomputable def WeierstrassCurve.av (E : WeierstrassCurve K) (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :
    ℤ :=
  Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal + 1 - numPointsReduction (v.valuation K).integer E

/-- The Frobenius angle `θ_v ∈ [0, π]` of a Weierstrass curve `E` over a number field `K` at a
finite place `v`, defined by `a_v(E) = 2 √q_v cos θ_v`. -/
noncomputable def WeierstrassCurve.theta (E : WeierstrassCurve K)
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) : ℝ :=
  frobeniusAngle (E.av v) (Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal)

/-- The finite places `v` of `K` of norm at most `X` at which `E` has good reduction. -/
def WeierstrassCurve.goodPlacesLE (E : WeierstrassCurve K) (X : ℕ) :
    Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :=
  {v | Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal ≤ X ∧ E.HasGoodReduction v}

/--

angles $\theta_v$ are equidistributed with respect to $\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$: for

section ModularForms

open CongruenceSubgroup ModularFormClass

variable {N : ℕ} {k : ℤ}

/-- The `n`-th Fourier coefficient `a_n(f)` of a cusp form `f` for `Γ₀(N)` at the cusp at
infinity, i.e. `f(τ) = ∑ a_n(f) e^{2πinτ}`. -/
noncomputable def modularFormAn (n : ℕ) (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) : ℂ :=
  (qExpansion 1 f).coeff n

local notation:73 "a_[" n:0 "]" f:72 => modularFormAn n f

/-- A cusp form `f` for `Γ₀(N)` is a *normalised Hecke eigenform* if `a_1(f) = 1` and its Fourier
coefficients satisfy the multiplicative relations of the Hecke eigenvalues (Diamond–Shurman,
Proposition 5.8.5, with trivial character): `a_{mn} = a_m a_n` for coprime `m, n`,
`a_{p^r} = a_p a_{p^{r-1}} - p^{k-1} a_{p^{r-2}}` for primes `p ∤ N` and
`a_{p^r} = a_p^r` for primes `p ∣ N`. -/
def IsNormalisedEigenform (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) : Prop :=
  a_[1] f = 1 ∧
  (∀ m n : ℕ, m.Coprime n → a_[m * n] f = a_[m] f * a_[n] f) ∧
  (∀ p r : ℕ, p.Prime → 2 ≤ r → ¬ p ∣ N →
    a_[p ^ r] f = a_[p] f * a_[p ^ (r - 1)] f - (p : ℂ) ^ (k - 1) * a_[p ^ (r - 2)] f) ∧
  ∀ p r : ℕ, p.Prime → 2 ≤ r → p ∣ N → a_[p ^ r] f = (a_[p] f) ^ r

/-- A cusp form `f` for `Γ₀(N)` has *complex multiplication* (Ribet) if it is fixed by the twist
by some non-trivial Dirichlet character `χ` modulo `M`, i.e. `χ(p) a_p(f) = a_p(f)` for all primes
`p ∤ N M`. Equivalently, `f` arises from a Hecke character of an imaginary quadratic field. -/
def CuspForm.HasComplexMultiplication (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : ℕ+) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ M), χ ≠ 1 ∧
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ¬ p ∣ N * M → χ p * a_[p] f = a_[p] f

/-- The angle `θ_p ∈ [0, π]` attached to a cusp form `f` of weight `k` for `Γ₀(N)` at a prime
`p`, defined by `a_p(f) = 2 p^{(k-1)/2} cos θ_p`. For a Hecke eigenform with trivial character
`a_p(f)` is real and, by Deligne's bound, `|a_p(f)| ≤ 2 p^{(k-1)/2}` for `p ∤ N`. -/
noncomputable def CuspForm.theta (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  arccos ((a_[p] f).re / (2 * (p : ℝ) ^ (((k : ℝ) - 1) / 2)))

/--
**Sato–Tate conjecture for modular forms.** Let $f = \sum a_n q^n$ be a normalised cuspidal Hecke
eigenform of weight $k \ge 2$ for $\Gamma_0(N)$ without complex multiplication. For a prime
$p \nmid N$ define $\theta_p \in [0, \pi]$ by $a_p = 2 p^{(k-1)/2} \cos\theta_p$. Then the angles
$\theta_p$ are equidistributed with respect to $\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$: for all
$0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{X \to \infty}
  \frac{\#\{p \le X : p \nmid N,\ \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le X : p \nmid N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta\,d\theta.$$

Proved by Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor (2011).
-/

    (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) (hf : IsNormalisedEigenform f)
    (hCM : ¬ f.HasComplexMultiplication) {α β : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β) (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun X : ℕ ↦
        ({p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ≤ X ∧ ¬ p ∣ N ∧ f.theta p ∈ Set.Icc α β}.ncard : ℝ) /
          {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ≤ X ∧ ¬ p ∣ N}.ncard)
      atTop (𝓝 (satoTateMeasure α β)) := by
  sorry

end ModularForms

/-!
# Sato–Tate conjecture

Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication. For a prime $p$
let $N_p$ be the number of points of $E$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ (including the point at infinity)
and define $\theta_p \in [0, \pi]$ by $p + 1 - N_p = 2\sqrt{p}\cos\theta_p$. The Sato–Tate
conjecture states that the angles $\theta_p$ are equidistributed with respect to the measure
$\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta \, d\theta$ on $[0, \pi]$: for all $0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\#\{p \le N : \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta \, d\theta.$$

The original conjecture and its generalisation to totally real fields were proved by Clozel,
Harris, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (2008) and Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor (2011).
The latter also proved the analogue for non-CM holomorphic newforms of weight at least two.
The generalisation to elliptic curves over arbitrary number fields is open.

## Formalisation notes

* Mathlib has no notion of complex multiplication for elliptic curves. We define an
  *endomorphism* of $E$ over an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$ as a group homomorphism of
  $E(\overline{K})$ that is given by two rational functions on $E$ (elements of the function
  field of $E$) at every affine point not mapped to the origin. Then $E$ has complex
  multiplication if it has an endomorphism that is not multiplication by an integer.
* We work with elliptic curves given by an integral Weierstrass equation (every elliptic curve
  is isomorphic to one, see `WeierstrassCurve.exists_isIntegral`), so that the reduction modulo
  a prime is the reduction of the coefficients. The Sato–Tate statements only depend on the
  isomorphism class of the curve and are insensitive to finitely many primes.
* Over $\mathbb{Q}$ we follow the article and average over all primes $p \le N$; at the finitely

/- ## Complex multiplication -/

section ComplexMultiplication

variable {L : Type*} [Field L]

/-- A rational function `f` on the Weierstrass curve `W` is regular at the affine point `(x, y)`
of `W` with value `c`: `f = a / b` for polynomial functions `a`, `b` on `W` with `b(x, y) ≠ 0`
and `a(x, y) = c * b(x, y)`. -/
def EvalsTo {W : Affine L} {x y : L} (h : W.Equation x y) (f : W.FunctionField) (c : L) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : W.CoordinateRing, f = algebraMap _ _ a / algebraMap _ _ b ∧
    AdjoinRoot.evalEval h b ≠ 0 ∧ AdjoinRoot.evalEval h a = c * AdjoinRoot.evalEval h b

/-- A map `φ` on the points of a Weierstrass curve `W` is *algebraic* if there are rational
functions `u`, `v` on `W` such that `φ P = (u(P), v(P))` for every affine point `P` of `W`
with `φ P ≠ 0`. For an elliptic curve `W` over an algebraically closed field, the algebraic
group homomorphisms `W.Point →+ W.Point` are exactly the endomorphisms of `W` (every rational
map between smooth projective curves extends to a morphism, and a morphism of elliptic curves is
the composite of an isogeny and a translation). -/
def IsAlgebraicMap (W : Affine L) (φ : W.Point → W.Point) : Prop :=
  ∃ u v : W.FunctionField,
    ∀ {x y : L} (h : W.Nonsingular x y) {x' y' : L} (h' : W.Nonsingular x' y'),
      φ (.some h) = .some h' → EvalsTo h.1 u x' ∧ EvalsTo h.1 v y'

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isAlgebraicMap_zero (W : Affine L) : IsAlgebraicMap W fun _ ↦ 0 := by
  refine ⟨0, 0, ?_⟩
  intro x y h x' y' h' hφ
  exact (Affine.Point.some_ne_zero h' hφ.symm).elim

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isAlgebraicMap_id (W : Affine L) : IsAlgebraicMap W id := by
  refine ⟨algebraMap _ _ (Affine.CoordinateRing.mk W (Polynomial.C Polynomial.X)),
    algebraMap _ _ (Affine.CoordinateRing.mk W Y), ?_⟩
  intro x y h x' y' h' hφ
  obtain ⟨rfl, rfl, -⟩ := Affine.Point.some.inj hφ
  refine ⟨⟨Affine.CoordinateRing.mk W (Polynomial.C Polynomial.X), 1, by simp, ?_, ?_⟩,
    ⟨Affine.CoordinateRing.mk W Y, 1, by simp, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · rw [map_one]; exact one_ne_zero
  · rw [map_one, mul_one, AdjoinRoot.evalEval_mk, Polynomial.evalEval_C, Polynomial.eval_X]
  · rw [map_one]; exact one_ne_zero
  · rw [map_one, mul_one, AdjoinRoot.evalEval_mk, Polynomial.evalEval_X]

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

open scoped Classical in
/-- An elliptic curve `E` over a field `K` has *complex multiplication* if, over an algebraic
closure `L` of `K`, it has an endomorphism (an algebraic group homomorphism `E(L) → E(L)`) that
is not multiplication by an integer. -/
def HasComplexMultiplication (E : WeierstrassCurve K) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : E⟮AlgebraicClosure K⟯ →+ E⟮AlgebraicClosure K⟯,
    IsAlgebraicMap _ φ ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ P, φ P ≠ n • P

end ComplexMultiplication

/- ## Elliptic curves over `ℚ` -/

section Rat

/-- The reduction modulo `p` of an elliptic curve over `ℚ` given by an integral Weierstrass
equation, as a Weierstrass curve over `ZMod p`. -/
noncomputable def reductionModPrime (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsIntegral ℤ] (p : ℕ) :
    WeierstrassCurve (ZMod p) :=
  (E.integralModel ℤ).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p))

/-- The Frobenius angle `θ_p ∈ [0, π]` of an elliptic curve `E` over `ℚ` at a prime `p`,
defined by $p + 1 - N_p = 2\sqrt{p}\cos\theta_p$, where `N_p` is the number of points of the
reduction of `E` modulo `p` (including the point at infinity). -/
noncomputable def frobeniusAngle (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsIntegral ℤ] (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  arccos (((p : ℤ) + 1 - Nat.card (reductionModPrime E p).toAffine.Point : ℤ) / (2 * √p))

@[category API, AMS 11 14]
theorem frobeniusAngle_mem_Icc (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsIntegral ℤ] (p : ℕ) :
    frobeniusAngle E p ∈ Set.Icc 0 π :=
  ⟨arccos_nonneg _, arccos_le_pi _⟩

/--
**Sato–Tate conjecture.** Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex
multiplication. For a prime $p$ let $N_p$ be the number of points of $E$ modulo $p$ and define
$\theta_p \in [0, \pi]$ by $p + 1 - N_p = 2\sqrt{p}\cos\theta_p$. Then for all real numbers
$0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\#\{p \le N : \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta \, d\theta.$$
This was proved by Clozel, Harris, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (2008) and Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty,
Harris and Taylor (2011).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 14]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic] [E.IsIntegral ℤ]
    (hE : ¬ HasComplexMultiplication E) (α β : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β)
    (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
      ({p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N ∧ frobeniusAngle E p ∈ Set.Icc α β}.ncard : ℝ) /
        {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N}.ncard)
      atTop (𝓝 (2 / π * ∫ θ in α..β, sin θ ^ 2)) := by
  sorry

end Rat

/- ## Elliptic curves over number fields -/

section NumberField

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]

/-- The reduction of an elliptic curve `E` over a number field `K`, given by a Weierstrass
equation with coefficients in `𝓞 K`, at a finite place `v` of `K`, as a Weierstrass curve
over the residue field `𝓞 K ⧸ v`. -/
noncomputable def reductionModPlace (E : WeierstrassCurve K) [E.IsIntegral (𝓞 K)]
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) : WeierstrassCurve (𝓞 K ⧸ v.asIdeal) :=
  (E.integralModel (𝓞 K)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk v.asIdeal)

/-- The Frobenius angle `θ_v ∈ [0, π]` of an elliptic curve `E` over a number field `K` at a
finite place `v` with residue field of size `q_v`, defined by
$q_v + 1 - N_v = 2\sqrt{q_v}\cos\theta_v$, where `N_v` is the number of points of the reduction
of `E` at `v` (including the point at infinity). -/
noncomputable def frobeniusAnglePlace (E : WeierstrassCurve K) [E.IsIntegral (𝓞 K)]
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) : ℝ :=
  arccos (((Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal : ℤ) + 1 -
    Nat.card (reductionModPlace E v).toAffine.Point : ℤ) / (2 * √(Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal)))

@[category API, AMS 11 14]
theorem frobeniusAnglePlace_mem_Icc (E : WeierstrassCurve K) [E.IsIntegral (𝓞 K)]
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) : frobeniusAnglePlace E v ∈ Set.Icc 0 π :=
  ⟨arccos_nonneg _, arccos_le_pi _⟩

/--
**Sato–Tate conjecture over totally real fields.** Let $E$ be an elliptic curve without complex
multiplication over a totally real number field $F$. For a finite place $v$ of good reduction
with residue field of size $q_v$, let $N_v$ be the number of points of $E$ modulo $v$ and
define $\theta_v \in [0, \pi]$ by $q_v + 1 - N_v = 2\sqrt{q_v}\cos\theta_v$. Then, ordering the
places by their norm, the angles $\theta_v$ are equidistributed with respect to
$\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta \, d\theta$: for all $0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{N \to \infty}
  \frac{\#\{v : q_v \le N,\ \alpha \le \theta_v \le \beta\}}{\#\{v : q_v \le N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta \, d\theta.$$
This was proved by Clozel, Harris, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (2008) under a mild assumption,
and in general by Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor (2011).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 14]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture.variants.totally_real [IsTotallyReal K]
    (E : WeierstrassCurve K) [E.IsElliptic] [E.IsIntegral (𝓞 K)]
    (hE : ¬ HasComplexMultiplication E) (α β : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β)
    (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
      ({v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) | (reductionModPlace E v).IsElliptic ∧
          Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal ≤ N ∧
          frobeniusAnglePlace E v ∈ Set.Icc α β}.ncard : ℝ) /
        {v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) | (reductionModPlace E v).IsElliptic ∧
          Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal ≤ N}.ncard)
      atTop (𝓝 (2 / π * ∫ θ in α..β, sin θ ^ 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
**Sato–Tate conjecture over number fields.** Let $E$ be an elliptic curve without complex
multiplication over a number field $K$. For a finite place $v$ of good reduction with residue
field of size $q_v$, let $N_v$ be the number of points of $E$ modulo $v$ and define

by their norm, the angles $\theta_v$ are equidistributed with respect to

  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta \, d\theta.$$
This is known for totally real fields and for CM fields, and open in general.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]

    (E : WeierstrassCurve K) [E.IsElliptic] [E.IsIntegral (𝓞 K)]
    (hE : ¬ HasComplexMultiplication E) (α β : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β)
    (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
      ({v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) | (reductionModPlace E v).IsElliptic ∧

/- ## Modular forms -/

section ModularForms

open CongruenceSubgroup ModularFormClass
open scoped UpperHalfPlane ModularForm CongruenceSubgroup

variable {N : ℕ} {k : ℤ}

/-- The `n`-th coefficient `a_n` of the `q`-expansion `f = ∑ a_n q^n`, `q = exp (2πiτ)`, of a
cusp form `f` for `Γ₀(N)`. -/
noncomputable def modularFormAn (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) (n : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  (qExpansion 1 f).coeff n

/-- A cusp form `f = ∑ a_n q^n` for `Γ₀(N)` of weight `k` is a *normalised eigenform* (for all
Hecke operators) if `a_1 = 1` and its coefficients satisfy the Hecke relations
`a_{mn} = a_m a_n` for coprime `m`, `n`, `a_{p^r} = a_p a_{p^{r-1}} - p^{k-1} a_{p^{r-2}}` for
primes `p ∤ N`, and `a_{p^r} = a_p^r` for primes `p ∣ N`. See Proposition 5.8.5 of
Diamond–Shurman. -/
def IsNormalisedEigenform (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) : Prop :=
  modularFormAn f 1 = 1 ∧
  (∀ m n : ℕ, m.Coprime n →
    modularFormAn f (m * n) = modularFormAn f m * modularFormAn f n) ∧
  (∀ p r : ℕ, p.Prime → 2 ≤ r → ¬ p ∣ N → modularFormAn f (p ^ r) =
    modularFormAn f p * modularFormAn f (p ^ (r - 1)) -
      (p : ℂ) ^ (k - 1) * modularFormAn f (p ^ (r - 2))) ∧
  (∀ p r : ℕ, p.Prime → 2 ≤ r → p ∣ N →
    modularFormAn f (p ^ r) = modularFormAn f p ^ r)

/-- A cusp form `f = ∑ a_n q^n` has *complex multiplication* if it is invariant under twisting
by some non-trivial Dirichlet character `χ`, that is, `a_p = χ(p) a_p` for all but finitely many
primes `p` (Ribet). -/
def IsCMForm (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) : Prop :=
  ∃ (D : ℕ) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ D), D ≠ 0 ∧ χ ≠ 1 ∧
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ χ p * modularFormAn f p ≠ modularFormAn f p}.Finite

/-- The Frobenius angle `θ_p ∈ [0, π]` of a cusp form `f = ∑ a_n q^n` of weight `k` at a prime
`p`, defined by $a_p = 2 p^{(k-1)/2} \cos\theta_p$. For an eigenform with trivial character the
coefficients `a_p` are real, so only the real part of `a_p` is used. -/
noncomputable def modularFormFrobeniusAngle (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  arccos ((modularFormAn f p).re / (2 * (p : ℝ) ^ (((k : ℝ) - 1) / 2)))

/--
**Sato–Tate conjecture for modular forms.** Let $f = \sum a_n q^n$ be a normalised cuspidal
Hecke eigenform of weight $k \ge 2$ for $\Gamma_0(N)$ without complex multiplication. For a prime
$p \nmid N$ define $\theta_p \in [0, \pi]$ by $a_p = 2p^{(k-1)/2}\cos\theta_p$ (which is possible
by Deligne's bound $|a_p| \le 2p^{(k-1)/2}$). Then the angles $\theta_p$, $p \nmid N$, are
equidistributed with respect to $\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta \, d\theta$: for all
$0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{X \to \infty}
  \frac{\#\{p \le X : p \nmid N,\ \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le X : p \nmid N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta \, d\theta.$$
This was proved by Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor (2011).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture.variants.modular_forms (hN : 0 < N) (hk : 2 ≤ k)
    (f : CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) (hf : IsNormalisedEigenform f) (hCM : ¬ IsCMForm f)
    (α β : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β) (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun X : ℕ ↦
      ({p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ¬ p ∣ N ∧ p ≤ X ∧
          modularFormFrobeniusAngle f p ∈ Set.Icc α β}.ncard : ℝ) /
        {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ¬ p ∣ N ∧ p ≤ X}.ncard)
      atTop (𝓝 (2 / π * ∫ θ in α..β, sin θ ^ 2)) := by
  sorry

end ModularForms

end SatoTateConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: Only minor points. (1) The notes suggest ModularityConjecture.lean's IsNormalisedEigenform/modularFormAn as the nearest idiom; however that file defines coefficients via `qExpansion N f`, which in Mathlib is the expansion in the parameter exp(2πiτ/N), so its `a_n` is actually a_{n/N} (zero unless N ∣ n). Reusing it would have been unfaithful; I redefined the coefficients with `qExpansion 1 f`. (2) The higher-genus slot as worded in the article omits the generic-monodromy hypothesis (as the notes acknowledge) and additionally requires curves of genus n over ℚ with finite-field point counts and Jacobian endomorphism rings, none of which exist in Mathlib; it is reported as missing_primitives rather than stated in a weakened (e.g. hyperelliptic-only, hypothesis-free) form.
modeling_decisions: Non-CM is formalised via a bespoke definition: E has CM iff over AlgebraicClosure K there is a group homomorphism of E(L) given by rational functions (at every affine point not sent to O) that is not [n] for any n : ℤ. Equivalence with End(E) ≠ ℤ uses standard facts (rational maps from smooth curves to projective curves extend to morphisms; a morphism E → E is a translation composed with an isogeny; a group homomorphism agreeing with a morphism off its kernel is that isogeny). Reviewers should check this argument.

Elliptic curves are taken with an integral Weierstrass equation ([E.IsIntegral ℤ] resp. [E.IsIntegral (𝓞 K)]) so the reduction is coefficient-wise; every elliptic curve is isomorphic to such a model (WeierstrassCurve.exists_isIntegral) and the statements depend only on the isomorphism class and are insensitive to finitely many primes. Mathlib's local minimal-model/reduction API was not usable because the required Algebra/IsFractionRing instances between Localization.AtPrime and ℚ (or K) do not exist.

Over ℚ the average is over ALL primes p ≤ N, as in the article's displayed formula. At the finitely many primes where the integral model reduces to a singular curve, N_p counts nonsingular affine points plus the point at infinity; this does not affect the limit. Over number fields (following the decomposition notes) the average is over finite places of good reduction of the model, ordered by absolute norm, in both numerator and denominator.
θ_p is defined with Real.arccos, which lands in [0, π] and is the unique solution of 2√p cos θ_p = p + 1 − N_p when the Hasse bound holds (always at good primes).

Counts are Set.ncard of sets of primes/places with bounded norm; these sets are finite (Ideal.finite_setOf_absNorm_le), so ncard is the true cardinality. The right-hand side is 2/π * ∫ θ in α..β, sin θ ^ 2 (interval integral), matching the article; closed intervals Set.Icc α β match α ≤ θ_p ≤ β.

Modular forms: restricted to trivial character (CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k) as in the decomposition notes; a_p is then real and the statement uses (a_p).re. Level N > 0 and weight k ≥ 2 are hypotheses. The eigenform hypothesis is the coefficient-relation version (normalised eigenform for all T_n), which is slightly broader than 'newform' but the statement remains true for such forms since their a_p for p ∤ N agree with those of a newform.

CM form is defined à la Ribet by twist invariance χ(p)a_p = a_p for all but finitely many primes with χ a non-principal Dirichlet character of modulus D ≠ 0 (D ≠ 0 excludes ZMod 0 = ℤ where all χ(p) vanish).
The q-expansion coefficients use qExpansion 1 f (expansion in e^{2πiτ}), not qExpansion N f as in ModularityConjecture.lean.

Categories: original conjecture, totally real variant and modular form variant are research solved (CHT 2008, BGHT 2011); the general number field variant is research open. The higher genus slot is omitted (missing primitives).
Basic API/test lemmas were added for the bespoke definitions (zero and identity maps are algebraic; Frobenius angles lie in [0, π]).

sato_tate_conjecture.why: Stated for E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ, [E.IsElliptic], [E.IsIntegral ℤ], ¬HasComplexMultiplication E, and 0 ≤ α < β ≤ π, as Tendsto of #{p prime ≤ N : θ_p ∈ [α,β]} / #{p prime ≤ N} to (2/π)∫_α^β sin²θ dθ, with θ_p = arccos((p+1−N_p)/(2√p)) and N_p = Nat.card of the (nonsingular) points, including the point at infinity, of the reduction mod p of the integral model. Needed bespoke definitions for complex multiplication and for the reduction/Frobenius angle.

sato_tate_conjecture.variants.higher_gen.why: Omitted. Mathlib has no usable notion of a smooth projective curve of genus n > 1 over ℚ (or a number field) with point counts over F_{p^r}, no unitarized L-polynomial / characteristic polynomial of Frobenius, and no Jacobian or endomorphism ring of a Jacobian. The notes correctly point out that the statement is only true under a generic-monodromy hypothesis (End(Jac C) = ℤ, Sato–Tate group all of USp(2n)), which cannot be expressed at all with existing primitives. USp(2n) and its Haar measure could be built from Matrix.unitaryGroup/symplecticGroup and MeasureTheory.Measure.haar, but the arithmetic side is entirely missing, so no faithful statement is possible.

statement_blocks.sato_tate_conjecture:
/--
**Sato–Tate conjecture.** Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex
multiplication. For a prime $p$ let $N_p$ be the number of points of $E$ modulo $p$ and define
$\theta_p \in [0, \pi]$ by $p + 1 - N_p = 2\sqrt{p}\cos\theta_p$. Then for all real numbers
$0 \le \alpha < \beta \le \pi$,
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\#\{p \le N : \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta \, d\theta.$$
This was proved by Clozel, Harris, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (2008) and Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty,
Harris and Taylor (2011).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 14]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic] [E.IsIntegral ℤ]
    (hE : ¬ HasComplexMultiplication E) (α β : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α < β)
    (hβ : β ≤ π) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
      ({p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N ∧ frobeniusAngle E p ∈ Set.Icc α β}.ncard : ℝ) /
        {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ≤ N}.ncard)
      atTop (𝓝 (2 / π * ∫ θ in α..β, sin θ ^ 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
**Sato–Tate conjecture for modular forms.** Let $f = \sum a_n q^n$ be a normalised cuspidal

$$\lim_{X \to \infty}
  \frac{\#\{p \le X : p \nmid N,\ \alpha \le \theta_p \le \beta\}}{\#\{p \le X : p \nmid N\}}
  = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta \sin^2\theta \, d\theta.$$
This was proved by Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris and Taylor (2011).
-/

multiplication over a number field $K$. For a finite place $v$ of good reduction with residue

import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.ModularityConjecture

/-!
# Sato–Tate conjecture

The Sato–Tate conjecture describes the distribution of Frobenius traces of a non-CM elliptic
curve. The original conjecture over the rationals, now a theorem, is stated below. Related
variants over number fields, for modular forms, and for higher-genus curves require arithmetic
geometry that is not yet available in Mathlib.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Sato–Tate conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sato%E2%80%93Tate_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace SatoTateConjecture

open Filter ModularityConjecture
open scoped Topology

/-- The rational $j$-invariants of elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with complex
multiplication. -/
def cmJInvariants : Finset ℚ :=
  {0, 1728, -3375, 8000, -32768, 54000, 287496, -884736, -12288000, 16581375,
    -884736000, -147197952000, -262537412640768000}

/-- A rational elliptic curve is non-CM exactly when its $j$-invariant is not one of the
thirteen rational CM $j$-invariants. -/
def IsNonCM (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic] : Prop :=
  E.j ∉ cmJInvariants

/-- The angle $\theta_p\in[0,\pi]$ obtained from the normalized trace of the reduction of
`E` modulo `p`. The point count used by `WeierstrassCurve.ap` is affine, so it already accounts
for the missing point at infinity in the formula $a_p=p+1-N_p$. -/
noncomputable def frobeniusAngle (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic] (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.arccos ((E.ap p : ℝ) / (2 * Real.sqrt p))

/-- The number of primes $p\le N$ for which $\theta_p$ lies in the closed interval
$[\alpha,\beta]$. -/
noncomputable def anglePrimeCount (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic]
    (α β : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.range (N + 1)).filter fun p ↦
    p.Prime ∧ α ≤ frobeniusAngle E p ∧ frobeniusAngle E p ≤ β).card

/--
The Sato–Tate conjecture (now a theorem): if $E/\mathbb Q$ is a non-CM elliptic curve and
$p+1-N_p=2\sqrt p\cos\theta_p$ with $0\le\theta_p\le\pi$, then for every
$0\le\alpha<\beta\le\pi$,
$$
 \lim_{N\to\infty}
 \frac{\#\{p\le N:\alpha\le\theta_p\le\beta\}}{\#\{p\le N\}}
 =\frac{2}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\beta\sin^2\theta\,d\theta.
$$
Here `WeierstrassCurve.ap` computes $p+1-N_p$ using an affine point count. Its possibly
exceptional values at the finitely many primes where the chosen rational equation has bad
reduction do not affect this limit.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 14]
theorem sato_tate_conjecture (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic] (hE : IsNonCM E) :
    ∀ α β : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α < β → β ≤ Real.pi →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (anglePrimeCount E α β N : ℝ) / N.primeCounting) atTop
        (𝓝 ((2 / Real.pi) * ∫ θ in α..β, Real.sin θ ^ 2)) := by
  sorry

end SatoTateConjecture
modeling_decisions: The terse list-page entry was expanded using the linked Sato–Tate article into its explicit closed-interval prime-count limit for a non-CM elliptic curve over Q.
Non-CM over Q is represented by exclusion of the 13 rational CM j-invariants. This is equivalent to the usual geometric non-CM condition specifically for elliptic curves defined over Q.
The Frobenius trace reuses `ModularityConjecture.WeierstrassCurve.ap`, whose affine point count gives p + 1 - N_p because the point at infinity is omitted from the affine count.

The angle is defined by `Real.arccos (a_p / (2 * sqrt p))`. At every good prime this is exactly the unique theta_p in [0, pi] from the source. The chosen rational Weierstrass model can produce exceptional values only at finitely many denominator or bad-reduction primes, which do not affect the limiting distribution.

The numerator uses `Finset.range (N + 1)` while the denominator uses `Nat.primeCounting N`; therefore both count primes p <= N. The source's closed interval alpha <= theta_p <= beta and bounds 0 <= alpha < beta <= pi are preserved literally.

The totally-real, arbitrary-number-field, modular-form, and higher-genus variants were not weakened to generic angle or matrix sequences, since doing so would erase the requirement that the data arise from the specified arithmetic-geometric objects.

sato_tate_conjecture.variants.higher_gen.why: A faithful Katz–Sarnak statement needs smooth projective curves of genus n, Jacobians and their endomorphisms (for the generic Sato–Tate-group hypothesis), good reduction and unitarized Frobenius L-polynomials, compact USp(2n), conjugacy classes, Haar probability measure, and equidistribution on the conjugacy quotient. Mathlib has separate symplectic and unitary matrix groups but not this combined arithmetic-geometric infrastructure.

sato_tate_conjecture.variants.modular_fo.why: Mathlib has cusp forms and q-expansions, and the repository has the ad hoc `ModularityConjecture.IsNormalisedEigenform`, but there is no adequate notion of holomorphic newform/Hecke eigenform or of a CM modular form. The existing normalized-eigenform predicate does not express newness and cannot faithfully support the stated quantification over arbitrary non-CM newforms.

sato_tate_conjecture.variants.number_fie.why: A faithful statement needs non-CM elliptic curves over arbitrary number fields together with finite-place good reduction, residue norm, and Frobenius point-count data tied to the curve. Those integrated primitives are absent.

sato_tate_conjecture.variants.totally_re.why: Mathlib has number fields, totally real fields, finite places, and local reduction ingredients, but lacks an integrated definition of the good reduction of a global elliptic curve at each finite place, its residue-field Frobenius trace/point count, and non-CM elliptic curves over a general number field. Replacing these by arbitrary supplied sequences would discard the essential arithmetic-geometric content.
